card.tagline: The steady straight dance of Kalymnos island festivals.
card.profile: The Isios Horos, known locally as the 'straight dance', is a traditional Greek folk dance originating from the island of Kalymnos. Performed at vibrant social gatherings and local festivals, it brings men and women together in an open circle. Bound by a crossed basket weave hand hold, the line maintains a steady basic step while the leader executes intricate improvisations. Moving to a 2/4 meter, the dance embodies the shared festivity of the Dodecanese islands.
card.insight: On the Aegean island of Kalymnos, dancers intertwine their hands in a basket weave formation to perform the Isios, a 2/4 rhythm open-circle dance where only the leader improvises.
card.profile_long:
The Isios Horos—translated directly by locals as the 'straight dance'—is a fundamental expression of social celebration on the Greek island of Kalymnos. Performed during regional festivals and community gatherings, the dance brings men and women together to celebrate their shared cultural heritage within the Dodecanese archipelago.

The dance is performed in an open circle structure, bringing the community into a shared physical space. Dancers bind themselves to one another using a crossed basket weave hand hold, creating a close-knit line that moves collectively. The steady rhythm of the dance is set in a 2/4 meter, providing a structured musical foundation for the circle's progression.

While the main body of dancers maintains the foundational basic step to uphold the collective structure, the lead dancer holds a special role. Positioned at the head of the open circle, the leader is granted the freedom to improvise on the steps, introducing creative variations and expressive flair while the rest of the line follows the continuous rhythm.

While the entire group performs a consistent basic step to maintain the circle, the leader at the head of the line improvises steps and variations.
